column1: # WP-T4 acceptance pins, read by accept.sh.
# One row per package the embryo harness builds. Each names a leaf small enough
# that a failure points at the runtime rather than at the package's own weight.
# bzip2 is first because it is the cleanest such leaf: pure C, no external
# library dependency, a hand-written Makefile rather than autotools, its own
# self-test built into `make test`, and a libc surface of forty symbols in the
# earliest-demand slices.
# The build line carries el8's effective flags rather than the naked Makefile.
# The vendor does not run `make CC=cc bzip2`; the pinned spec wraps the same
# Makefile in CFLAGS="$RPM_OPT_FLAGS ..." and LDFLAGS="%{__global_ldflags}",
# and on el8 those macros pull in the redhat-rpm-config hardening specs that
# have made RHEL userland position-independent by default since the RHEL 8 line.
# Building without them produced an ET_EXEC at 0x400000 that the vendor does
# not ship, which is what WP-56 spent a session parked on. The two -specs=
# arguments are replaced here by the flags those specs files inject, because
# the specs files are Red Hat's rpm configuration and are not in this sysroot;
# that substitution is S2 in doc/substitutions.md, and the chain behind it is
# measured in spike/vendor-hardened-build/.
# The bzip2-nonpie row is deliberately red. A minority of el8 opts out of
# hardening with %undefine _hardened_build, and prebuilt vendor ET_EXECs exist,
# so fixed-address loading is still owed even though bzip2 no longer needs it.
# The row builds the same source through the naked Makefile to get a genuine
# non-PIE image, and it stays red until DR-0072's low-window contract holds.
# Do not silence it by dropping the row; see doc/decisions/0072-*.md.
# Columns, TAB-separated:
#   name     the package, and the name to pass accept.sh
#   relpath  its .src.rpm under the mirror root
#   sha256   the pin; a fetch whose hash differs is refused
#   build    the build command, %CC% replaced by the cross compiler, run from
#            the unpacked source directory; it must leave the binary below
#   binary   the built executable to read the libc surface from
# name<TAB>relpath<TAB>sha256<TAB>build<TAB>binary
bzip2
bzip2-nonpie
